The `data/*.json` changes are just refreshed pricing/recommendation output from the live run (expected side effect of running the app), not something I need to revert.

## Summary

Moved the two standalone scripts into `src/` and wired them directly into the app instead of spawning them as subprocesses:

- [scripts/fetch-artificial-analysis.ts](scripts/fetch-artificial-analysis.ts) → [src/artificial-analysis/fetch.ts](src/artificial-analysis/fetch.ts), refactored into an exported `fetchArtificialAnalysisData()` function.
- [scripts/compute-scores.ts](scripts/compute-scores.ts) → [src/scoring/compute-scores.ts](src/scoring/compute-scores.ts), refactored into an exported `computeScores()` function.
- [src/index.ts](src/index.ts) now imports and calls both directly, removing the `node:child_process` spawn helper entirely.
- [package.json](package.json) `start` script uses `--env-file-if-exists=.env` so `AA_API_KEY` loads in-process (needed now that the fetch runs in the same process, not a spawned one with its own `--env-file`), while preserving the existing friendly "missing .env" error message.
- Deleted the now-empty `scripts/` directory.

Verified with a full `npm start` run — all four steps execute in one process and `data/recommendations.json` is produced correctly.
